newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam says set to edge open the Internet door.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam says set to edge open the Internet door.

text.p: Vietnam said on Tuesday it was hoping to license its first Internet provider within weeks as part of a step-by-step opening to the information superhighway.
An official at the Directorate General of Post and Telecommunications told Reuters the basic infrastructure to enable Vietnam to go on line was already in place.
"So, this is the biggest step for us so far," he said.
Vice-Minister of Science and Technology, Chau Hao, was quoted in the Lao Dong newspaper on Monday as saying Vietnam planned to open two gateways -- one in Hanoi and one in Ho Chi Minh City.
He indicated the initial service would be available through one provider only, but added that access would be gradually opened up over time.
"We will expand access in accordance with our ability to control the technology," he said. "The regulations have to be in step with scientific development and social demands."

Vietnam's communist government has been slow to allow popular access to the Internet, but domestic intranet services, which also provide delayed e-mail access to the web, have been available for some time.

Delegates at a seminar last week in Ho Chi Minh City said the government's prime concern was preventing subversive or other harmful material from being circulated in Vietnam, received from abroad, or sent overseas.
